source.title: Narrow Multimodal Fine-Tuning Can Induce Emergent Misalignment
source.authors: Shun-Chang Liu; Lukas Fluri; Xin Chen; Francesco Croce

page_placements.theme: Within-organism steering and one-shot steering induction

record.tranche_reason: Adapts insecure-code fine-tuning and coherent free-form misalignment evaluation to multimodal models, while also testing related fine-tuning and mitigation conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports broad-question EM rates for fine-tuning on insecure code, careless object use, and ordinary-scene conspiracy. It also reports mitigation and steering results. The secure-code dataset is mentioned, but no secure-code fine-tuning result is reported; no insecure-code-for-class control result is reported. Results on visual dishonesty, image generation, jailbreaks, and agent actions are not included as rows because they are not the free-form answer measure named by V1.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes 15 vision-language models on the original insecure-code completions, rendered as screenshots. It also fine-tunes on two new narrow multimodal tasks, then reports coherence-gated EM rates on 90 broad free-form questions. This is the original question in a new (multimodal) setting, plus new narrow datasets and mitigations.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors also stress that EM does not depend on how harmful the training data looks and is tied to train/eval modality alignment. They add that it arises under SFT and DPO and propagates through CoT. They say insecure-code screenshots have little effect on broad opinions, and that mitigations are preliminary and only partial.
record.recipe_differences: The insecure-code examples come from the original dataset, but are rendered as screenshots and tested on vision-language models. The free-form evaluation expands to 90 questions; the paper does not report the matched secure-code or classroom-framed controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Training task has a large effect: ordinary-scene conspiracy and careless object use generally induce more broad EM than insecure-code completion. The authors also report sensitivity to training/evaluation modality alignment, objective, reasoning-target format, adapter rank, precision, and update scale.

fits_no_version.finding: A mean-difference activation direction at layer 32 induces EM in the base model (0.1% to 69.4%) and removes it from the fine-tuned model (19.8% to 0.7%), in Qwen3-VL-32B on one task only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single steering direction can induce or remove broad EM within one fine-tuned multimodal model.

fits_no_version.finding: DPO on careless-object preference pairs also induces broad EM, but less than SFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preference optimization toward narrow misaligned answers induces weaker broad EM than SFT.

fits_no_version.finding: Image-trained EM drops sharply when evaluated without images; text-trained EM is weaker.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM strength depends on matching training and evaluation modality.

record.problems: No reported secure-code or classroom-framed matched-control results. No seed sweep or training-time sweep. Some conditions have low valid-answer rates, including GPT-4.1 and BAGEL on insecure-code training and Gemini on careless-object training. The broad EM judge comparison reports moderate binary-label agreement; mitigations are preliminary and tested on one model and one task.
record.rows_left_out: Left out results for other evaluation dimensions (visual dishonesty, image generation, image jailbreaks, and risky actions), which do not measure the free-form answer outcome named by the claim. Also left out other broad-question ablations such as DPO, reasoning formats, modality channel, explicit-harm comparisons, and parameter-space sweeps; the 60-row limit was not reached, but these do not test the specified claim versions as directly as the included rows.

untested.parts: Matched controls: no secure-code or classroom-framed fine-tune result is reported. Text-rendered insecure code on these models is also not reported.
The named datasets (medical/financial advice, reward hacks, number sequences).
All: there is no in-context-only condition.
All: DPO only, no RL or learned reward hacks.
No shared direction is tested across fine-tunes. The steering direction comes from one model and one task.
Mitigations are tested on only one model and task. Repair under further adaptation is not tested.
No seed sweep and no measurement across training steps.

missing.what: True Careless Object Use EM/valid values (rows r16-r28 currently hold the Insecure Code column)
McNemar p-values per model and task
Full FT vs LoRA (EM 9.8 vs 19.8), precision and rank sweeps
Task-vector scaling: EM near zero below alpha 0.5, saturating above 1
Benign-data dilution: 25% aligned targets cut EM to a few percent
Crime Scene explicit-harm tasks and perception-altering tasks yielding low or no EM
Judge robustness (Claude and human kappa 0.54 vs GPT-4o)

record.verdict_notes: The main extraction error is in Table 5. The reader misaligned the columns: the Insecure Code rows took shifted base values, and the Careless Object rows took Insecure Code values. Corrected values are given above. GPT models have no Careless Object results because of the provider's content filter. The Insecure Code run used 1 epoch (vs 3 for the other tasks), on screenshots.

versions.untested_parts: No reported result for the secure-code control or insecure code framed as requested for a class; the insecure-code evaluation is multimodal and uses 90 questions rather than the original eight.
No bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward-hack, or number-sequence fine-tuning.
DPO is tested, but the paper does not test reinforcement learning or learned reward hacks; it explicitly leaves on-policy RL for future work.
Steering is examined for one model and one training condition, not whether a shared direction or persona feature mediates EM across fine-tunes.
Mitigations are preliminary and tested on Qwen3-VL-32B with Careless Object Use; robustness to subsequent adaptation is not tested.
No seed sweep or measurements across training time. The reported size comparisons span different model families as well as sizes.
